correctness.rationale: For Cr_n (n>=3), if p,q denote white vertices in A,B, every blue b_i sees p-1_{i in I} whites and every blue a_i sees q-1_{i in J}. If p>=3, no blue B-vertex can force into A; any opposite-direction forces leave p unchanged, hence a forcing set has p<=2, and symmetrically q<=2, so |S|>=2n-4. At equality, p=q=2. Identical omitted index pairs I=J give no initial force; distinct pairs admit explicit alternating forces filling their differing indices and then final two whites. Thus ALL minima omit distinct two-subsets on respective shores; count binom(n,2)(binom(n,2)-1). Independently enumerated all size-(2n-4) sets and all smaller near-minimum sets on n=3..9, obtaining counts 6,30,90,210,420,756,1260 and no contrary examples. This recovers the prior scalar formula but novelty is the full classification/count.
residual_risks: Only n>=3; initial finite color-change exhaustions are corroboration, not an all-n proof.
This is standard zero forcing, not PSD or skew variants.
